A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same QFR research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: Section 6 and Figures 1–2 report original exploitability experiments on four benchmark games.

after.justification: Section 5 and Figures 1–2 report original game experiments; Appendix H and Figure 3 additionally report a neural-network ablation.

M1.justification: The trajectory-Q estimator, bidilated regularizer, optimistic updates, exploration constraints, and lazy variant are retained. Algorithm 1 reformulates the tabular updates using value-function and log-gradient notation. The neural experiment does not specify a distinct proposed QFR algorithm.

E1.justification: Both evaluate four-sided Liar’s Dice, Leduc Poker, Kuhn Poker, and 2×2 Abrupt Dark Hex. The new neural ablation reuses Leduc Poker. Stratego is added as motivation, not as an evaluated game.

E2.justification: Figure 1 adds BalancedOMD (BOMD) and BalancedFTRL (BFTRL) across all four games to v1’s CFR, CFR+, and MMD comparisons. These are newly evaluated comparators, although their source papers were already cited.

E3.justification: Figure 1 extends the iteration horizon from 10^6 to 10^7. Figure 2 extends the poker and Hex horizons from 10^5 to 10^6, retaining the short Liar’s Dice horizon. Added protocols include neural approximation with gradient clipping at 0.5 and BOMD/BFTRL tuning with exploration parameter η/20.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained tabular feedback comparisons, Figure 3 adds a neural Leduc Poker ablation contrasting counterfactual and trajectory-Q feedback. Exploitability and pre-clipping gradient norms test whether importance sampling destabilizes neural training despite gradient clipping.

E5.justification: Both Figure 1 captions report 100 repetitions with different seeds, and both versions display shaded variability. No new significance tests or defined uncertainty-estimation procedure are introduced; Figure 3 does not specify a separate run-count protocol.

E6.justification: Figures 1–2 replace performance curves under longer budgets. Figure 1’s reported exceptions against CFR/CFR+ in Liar’s Dice and MMD in Hex disappear; v2 instead reports Liar’s Dice exploitability of 0.174 for QFR versus 0.167 for BFTRL. Neural stability results are added. These are revised-setting results, not demonstrated same-setting gains.

T1.justification: The main convergence theorems and rates remain. Local corrections include opponent-reach factors in Equation (4.3) and the entropy stability constant in Equation (C.4). However, v2 replaces v1’s concluding Bregman derivation in Appendix D.1 and concentration inequality in Appendix E with an unrelated identity in E.1 and a repeated expectation identity in F, leaving gaps in the displayed proofs.

C1.justification: The central first-policy-gradient and best-iterate convergence claims remain. The rewritten conclusion narrows v1’s separate first-ever claims about stochastic-feedback learning and avoiding importance sampling to achieving the three desiderata jointly.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations involving optimism, regularization, importance-sampling instability, and multiplicative noise relative to PCFR+. It removes the conclusion’s explicit discussion of unresolved polynomial game-size dependence and lazy updates’ impracticality outside tabular games. The experimental learning-rate mismatch with theory remains acknowledged.

D1.justification: v2 removes Table 2’s explicit hyperparameter grids and selection rule, referring to supplementary material whose grids are absent from the supplied PDF. It adds PPO/CleanRL implementation information, neural-experiment hardware and clipping details, and a direct baselines-code locator rather than only the existing library link.

R1.justification: v2 adds LocalOMD and six references supporting related work, motivation, regularization, and implementation. Table 1 and Appendix A qualify ARMAC/ACH sampling requirements and add criticism of ACH’s equilibrium convergence. The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Related work moves to Appendix A, while a rewritten conclusion moves into main Section 6. The title specifies best-iterate convergence, and algorithm explanations and proof roadmaps are expanded. Most technical exposition is retained.

P2.justification: The paper adopts ICLR formatting, restructures Table 1 and Algorithm 1, redraws Figures 1–2 with changed axes and legends, adds Figure 3, and removes Table 2. Figure 2 also loses the dashed Q-feedback legend entry despite retaining dashed curves.

improvement.justification: The added baseline comparisons and neural ablation strengthen empirical support. However, v2 removes reproducibility settings and replaces valid proof steps with unrelated or repeated identities in Appendix E.1, page 27, and Appendix F, page 29. These losses weaken theoretical traceability and reproducibility. The material benefits and harms do not establish a reliable net direction in overall quality.
